title: CDC: Slow → Fast Level + Edge
constraints: `d_slow` comes from a slower, unrelated clock domain and is asynchronous to `clk_fast`. It stays stable for at least 2 `clk_fast` periods.
`q` is `d_slow` passed through a **2-flop synchronizer**: q = the value of `d_slow` sampled at the 2nd-most-recent rising edge of `clk_fast`.
`rise` is high for exactly **one** `clk_fast` cycle per rising edge of `q` (the cycle in which `q` has just become 1). It's computed from the synchronized signal, never from raw `d_slow`.
Synchronous reset (in the `clk_fast` domain) clears all flops. Must be synthesizable.
hints: Three flops: `s1 <= d_slow; s2 <= s1; s3 <= s2;` then `q = s2` and `rise = s2 & ~s3`.
Never use `d_slow` in any logic before it has passed through both synchronizer flops. The first flop may be metastable.
Slow to fast is the easy direction: the fast clock is guaranteed to see every level. Fast to slow needs a handshake.
